items.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: You’d hear, they mixed it up quite a bit. It wasn’t so personal now.

ctx.x: I guess I’m meaning things like that would be on the AM radio at the time, either the beginnings of rock & roll, I guess I’m moving later into the 50s or “How Much is that Doggie in the Window” kind of things that were hits back then. Did they have any influence?

Probably not. They probably pushed me into the direction of real jazz. And get that away from me. Doggie in the Window. There was, well you know you’d turn the radio on and you’d hear Doggie in the Window and the next thing would be a Benny Goodman tune or a Tommy Dorsey big band thing or some small group. You’d hear, they mixed it up quite a bit. It wasn’t so personal now.
Yeah. So that was really part of the pop music, popular.
